title: 3.8.23 Lab: Adapt the Pattern to a List
description: Apply the save/load pattern to an array of records rather than a single object, and read one record's field back out. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build a list of records
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it records; use any name that fits) holding an array of at least two objects. Each object should describe one thing with a name and a value.

steps.title: Save the whole list
steps.instructions: Use JSON.stringify on the array and store it with localStorage.setItem under a key.

steps.title: Load it back
steps.instructions: Read the key with localStorage.getItem, then parse it back into an array (the lesson calls it restored) using JSON.parse. An array round-trips exactly like an object.

steps.title: Prove it is a real array again
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the restored array's length and one record's field, confirming the array and its objects came back whole.

requirements.title: List saved by key
requirements.hint: Store the list with localStorage.setItem under a key of your choice.

requirements.title: Converted with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: The store holds text, so run the list through JSON.stringify first.

requirements.title: List restored with parse
requirements.description: Calls JSON.parse on the saved list. Help: 3.8.8 (JSON.parse — Text Back to Object)
requirements.hint: Read the key with getItem and turn the text back into an array with JSON.parse.

requirements.title: Restored list logged
requirements.hint: Print the restored array's length and one record's field.

requirements.title: restored is a separate array rebuilt from storage
requirements.description: restored is an array holding the same records as records, rebuilt from the text stored under a key, and the length and one record's field were printed. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: Save JSON.stringify(records) under a key, read it back with getItem and rebuild restored with JSON.parse. Print restored.length and a field of one record.

NEAR(x, y) : JSON.stringify(x) === JSON.stringify(y); const SAMEA = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[i])); const CONTIG = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length > 0 && a.length <= b.length && b.some((_, at) => at + a.length <= b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[at + i]))); const JEQ = (a, b) => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b); const PRINTS = (J, vs) => vs.every((x) => typeof x === 'number' ? Object.values(v).reduce((a, x) => a.concat(LEAVES(x)), []) : [v]; const JSONS = (t) => { const found = []; const txt = String(t).slice(0, 20000); for (let i = 0; i < txt.length && found.length < 40; i++) { if (txt[i] !== '{' && txt[i] !== '[') continue; let d = 0; let q = false; for (let j = i; j < txt.length; j++) { const ch = txt[j]; if (q) { if (ch === '\\') j++; else if (ch === '"') q = false; continue; } if (ch === '"') q = true; else if (ch === '{' || ch === '[') d++; else if (ch === '}' || ch === ']') { d--; if (d === 0) { try { found.push(JSON.parse(txt.slice(i, j + 1))); } catch (e) { } break; } } } } return found; }; return (Array.isArray(records) && records.length >= 2 && Array.isArray(restored) && JSON.stringify(restored) === JSON.stringify(records) && PRINTS(output.join(' '), [restored.length]) && restored.some(($r) => $r !== null && typeof $r === 'object' && Object.values($r).some(($v) => (typeof $v === 'string' || typeof $v === 'number') && PRINTS(output.join(' '), [$v]))) && !same('restored', 'records') && (() => { for (let $i = 0; $i < localStorage.length; $i++) { try { if (JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(localStorage.key($i)))) === JSON.stringify(records)) return true; } catch (e) { } } return false; })()); })()
checks.fail: restored should be an array rebuilt from the text you stored under a key with setItem, with the same records as records, and you should print its length and one record's field.

requirements.title: restored is parsed from what was stored, and a field is printed from it
requirements.description: When records holds other values, restored changes with it, and a console.log that runs prints one record's field from restored. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: Print restored.length and one field such as restored[0].name. Text typed in by hand does not change when records does.
